title: Diwali Gift Ideas: 18 Gifts for Family, Friends, and Hosts
summary: Diwali gift ideas sorted by who they're for: mithai and diyas for the host, a puja thali or a small gold bar for family, and what to bring to a party.
body_markdown:
ince


One gift and no time? Get a box of mithai. It works for a host you've met twice, the neighbors, the office, your own grandmother. Past that, it really depends who it's for. Britannica sums up Diwali as a time for[exchanging gifts, wearing new clothes and visiting friends and family](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Diwali-Hindu-festival) , and what you bring a host is not what you'd give your little brother or a six-year-old. So we've grouped the ideas by person. Hosts first.


## For the host of a Diwali party


### 1. Mithai, in a mixed box


The default. A good one, too.[Most families celebrate with sweets and food](https://www.hinduamerican.org/diwali) . A guest who walks in with kaju katli, besan ladoo and a few kinds of barfi is doing exactly what the evening calls for. Buy from an Indian sweet shop if there's one near you. The supermarket boxes aren't really the same thing.


Go mixed rather than one kind. Somebody else may already have brought the kaju katli.


### 2. Diyas or a set of candle holders


Clay diyas are Diwali's lamps (Diwali is named for rows of them). A host can go through dozens in one night. A set of hand-painted diyas, or brass holders that take a tealight, gets used the same evening. It is also the rare gift a host can set out while you're still in the doorway.


### 3. Dry fruits in a gift box


Cashews, almonds, pistachios, dates, maybe figs, in a tray or a painted tin. Yes, it's the predictable one. It also keeps for weeks, and when a house gets six boxes of sweets in two days, the thing that won't go stale by Thursday looks pretty good.


### 4. Good tea, or a spice box


If the host cooks: loose-leaf chai, a masala dabba (that round steel box with the little bowls inside), or saffron. A gram or two of saffron sounds like nothing. It isn't, by weight it's one of the priciest things in the kitchen. Handy when it's a coworker's family and you've never met them.


## For family


### 5. A puja thali set


The plate that holds what the family uses for Lakshmi Puja on the main night: a diya, kumkum, rice, a small bell, incense. Sets come in steel, brass and silver-plated finishes. Good for a couple in their first home. Also for the relative who's been using a dinner plate for years and hasn't noticed.


### 6. New clothes for the day


Wearing something new at Diwali is a custom in its own right. Clothing fits here easily. A kurta, a silk dupatta, a saree for someone whose taste you know well. Not sure of sizes? A dupatta, since it fits everyone.


### 7. A PAMP Diwali gold bar


On Dhanteras, the festival's first day, buying gold is one of the big customs (more in our[guide to what families buy on Dhanteras](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-to-buy-on-dhanteras) ). A small bar is that custom, wrapped. Quick note: we run Collect Pure, a marketplace for bullion and coins, and the gold and silver links here go to listings there.


The Swiss refiner PAMP Suisse puts Lakshmi on the front of its Diwali bars. The art around her is different every year. Peacocks in 2024. Rangoli the year after, and for 2026 it's the sacred cow. Every one is .9999 fine (24 karat). Each comes sealed in an assay card with the weight and fineness printed on it. Leave the card sealed when you give it. You can see the bar through the little window anyway.


If it's for one person, start with the[5 gram](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/5-gram-pamp-diwali-gold-bar-9999-fine-sealed-in-assay000343) or the[10 gram](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/10-gram-pamp-diwali-gold-bar-9999-fine-sealed-in-assay000344) . A full ounce is a lot more than most people spend on a present; five grams is about a sixth of that, ten about a third. You can see every Diwali design at once on[this page](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/diwali-gold-bars) . Price is the gold at live spot plus a premium, which the Pure app shows on every listing. On a small bar, more of what you pay is premium.


### 8. The 25 gram Lakshmi Multigram


This one's for giving to a whole family at once, say from the grandparents. PAMP's[Multigram](https://www.pamp.com/product/minted-ingots/diwali-rangoli-art-pure-gold-multigram25) puts 25 one-gram units on a single card, and PAMP registers and seals each one individually. On each little gram, Lakshmi is framed in marigolds and hibiscus. Rangoli covers the card. About 80% of an ounce in total. Check the photos on[our Multigram listing](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/25-gram-pamp-suisse-diwali-lakshmi-multigram-gold-bar-new-in-assay0139) for the design.


Before anything ships, we test it ourselves, and only what passes goes out as Pure Qualified. Shipping's insured, both directions, to $125,000. If you're curious how the designs have changed, our[PAMP Diwali Lakshmi bar guide](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/pamp-diwali-lakshmi-gold-bar) goes year by year.


### 9. Brass for the home


Maybe an urli, that wide shallow brass bowl with flowers and floating candles in it. Or a bell, or a lamp stand. Brass darkens over time and some people polish it back every Diwali along with the rest of the house. Handy for the parent or in-law who's impossible to shop for.


### 10. Something for your sibling on Bhai Dooj


The last day of the Diwali season belongs to siblings.[Bhai Beej, or Bhai Dooj,](https://www.hinduamerican.org/diwali/diwali-day-6) is for all siblings, "blood or chosen family," as the Hindu American Foundation puts it, with a meal together, sweets and gifts. What to give? Whatever that particular sibling would actually like. Personal wins over impressive here.


## For friends


### 11. Rangoli colors and stencils


Rangoli are the colored patterns people make at the doorway,[from flowers, powder, rice or sand](https://www.hinduamerican.org/diwali) . A few colors of powder, some stencils, a shaker. Great for a friend's first Diwali, or anyone whose kids will insist on helping.


### 12. A 1 ounce silver round


You'll often find a silver coin tucked into Diwali gift boxes, and on Dhanteras silver is bought alongside gold. A[1 ounce .999 fine silver round](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/1-oz-silver-round-accredited-brand-999-fine-random-design000260) is a full ounce of metal at a normal gift budget, since silver costs a fraction of what gold does. The listing is "random design," meaning the design varies and you get whichever accredited round fills the order. It won't carry a Diwali motif. Hold it by the edge. Silver tones where fingers touch it.


### 13. Donate in their name


Diwali is[a time for dana, charitable giving](https://www.hinduamerican.org/diwali) . Give to a cause your friend cares about and tell them in a card. It suits Diwali better than a lot of things in a shop. It's the right call for the friend who keeps saying they don't need anything.


## For kids


### 14. A 1 gram gold bar


A child's first piece of gold. A gram is roughly 1/31 of a troy ounce (3.2%), and a bar that size is smaller than a postage stamp, sealed in the same kind of assay card as the larger ones. The Diwali designs start at 5 grams. So at one gram it's a plain bar from an accredited refiner. See[gold bars from 1 gram up](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/gold-bars) .


### 15. Picture books about Diwali or the Ramayana


The story of Rama's return to Ayodhya is the one many families tell at Diwali, and there are versions for most ages, from board books to chapter books. For kids growing up in the US, where the school calendar may not mention the festival at all, a book they can read themselves goes a long way.


### 16. Clay diyas to paint


Plain clay diyas plus paints and brushes. Kids paint them in the afternoon, the family lights them that night. Of all the kids' ideas, this one gets them involved in the festival itself.


## For coworkers and neighbors


### 17. Individual boxes of sweets or dry fruits


For an office, several little boxes beat one big one on a table that empties by 10 a.m. If you have many coworkers, one shared tray of mithai plus a note saying what the occasion is will do. A manager or a client gets a single good dry fruit box.


### 18. Sweets and a diya for next door


Neighbors who don't celebrate will usually appreciate being included. A lit diya on the step and a plate of sweets with a short note ("Happy Diwali from number 12") is a warm gesture, and it answers the question of why your house has lights up this time of year.


## Frequently asked questions


### Do you bring a gift to a Diwali party?


Yes, something small. Sweets, dry fruits or a box of diyas is enough. Guests rarely arrive empty-handed. You don't need to match what the host gives guests, if they give anything.


### What do you give a neighbor for Diwali?


Sweets, almost always. A box or a plate, dropped off in the day or two before the main night, with a note if they don't celebrate. The point is including them.


### What are traditional Diwali gifts?


Sweets first. Then dry fruits, diyas and new clothes, with gold or silver bought around Dhanteras, and a puja thali or brass for the home. Most of what's newer, hampers and scented candles included, is a variation on those.


### Can you send gold as a Diwali gift within the US?


Yes. A sealed 5 or 10 gram bar ships insured to US addresses. Leave room for delivery if the gift has a date. For gifts outside the festival,[our list of gold and silver gift ideas](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/gold-and-silver-gift-ideas) goes from junk silver to graded Morgan dollars.
